correctness.rationale: The full Walsh spectrum and exact Hamming-shell transform prove the positive kernel formulas for all dimensions. Coefficientwise polynomial identities, Descartes-root counts with rational sign witnesses, and positive denominators certify the complete dimensions 1–5 classification. Shortest-path powers and the fifth Taylor coefficient give the universal small-step obstruction; a binomial monotonicity identity gives negativity at h=3/2, and the zero-mode limit yields eventual strict positivity. Exact rational full-matrix inversion was checked independently through dimension five with 12,593 assertions, supplementary to the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the method definition nor general positivity nonuniversality implies the exact two algebraic connected components of safe positive steps in dimension four, the three positive-step components including the isolated zero in dimension five, or the uniform fifth-distance small-step coefficient. originality.rationale: The new content is the sharp all-dimensional hypercube cutoff with exact four- and five-dimensional algebraic phase domains, not generic Runge–Kutta order barriers or the Walsh spectrum. Searches of the public mathematical literature and published searchable research records found no statement implying these windows; the named closest sources have distinct quantifiers, objectives, stability functions, or graphs. The unresolved risk of older specialized work is recorded explicitly.
residual_risks: Unindexed or earlier work could have studied the same fixed Radau IIA hypercube endpoint matrix in equivalent Krawtchouk notation.
The 1999 historical Radau survey was accessible only via publisher abstract and excerpts, not its entire full text.
Finite samples and failed searches are not uniqueness certificates; the claimed originality is qualified to the inspected primary material and published searchable research records.

value.rationale: The Boolean hypercube is a canonical Cartesian-product diffusion network, so an exact dimensional positivity threshold and safe timestep windows directly address whether a commonly used L-stable third-order method can represent nonnegative mass transport. The surprising arbitrarily-small-step failure beginning at Hamming distance five and the separated recovery windows in dimension five are natural structural boundaries rather than arbitrary examples or a tiny numerical improvement. The result supplies exact implementable restrictions without claiming a global theorem for other graph families.
